home.short: The start page: what waits on you, which agents are working, and what they said to each other.
home.more: It refreshes itself every minute. Click an agent card to watch that agent live.

flows.short: The page of every flow: the plan each agent writes as it works, with the questions that wait on you at the top.

flow.short: One piece of work an agent plans out as a small chart: steps, checks, asks and notes, joined in the order they happen.
flow.more: Agents write flows with the factory command line. You answer the asks and tick what you have checked; the rest is the agent's to update.

qa.short: The page of every ticket that passed QA, the last check before a push: its report, its screenshots and the steps to test it yourself.
qa.more: QA tests each change that touched code, writes a short report, and pushes the branch at the very commit it tested. A failure goes back to the agent that made the change.

script.short: The SCRIPT Generator: write a rough idea and get back a ready-to-paste prompt for any AI, in six labelled parts: Situation, Character, Request, Intent, Presentation and Tone.
script.more: Each Generate is one paid run of Opus 5.5 at high effort, with no tools and none of your settings. When the idea leaves gaps that matter, it asks a few short questions first (at most five at a time, in at most two rounds); say just do it to skip them.

tickets.short: The page for a ticket collection: the grid of who built what and how far it got, and the tables of every ticket below it.

timeline.short: A chart of what every agent did over time, one lane per agent, so you can see who worked on what and when.

agents.short: The page that lists every Claude Code session the dashboard found, with its subagents underneath.

subagents.short: The page that lists every subagent a session started to do one task: what it is working on, how it went, and its final report.
subagents.more: A builder worked in a worktree or made a commit; a lookup only read or searched. A subagent is stuck when it has not finished and has written nothing for 15 minutes, and stopped when it ended without a final report.

agent.short: A Claude Code session working in the repo. The coding agents usually work in their own worktree.
agent.more: One agent page shows its live transcript: each tool it ran, what it read and wrote, and its messages.

ask.short: A question an agent puts to you inside a flow. The agent stops at it until you answer Yes, No or a short text.
ask.more: In the rail, Ask opens the chat drawer, where you can talk to Independent about anything on the page.

alerts.short: Small pop-up notes when something needs you: a new ask, an agent that stopped, an answer that was not delivered. The bell keeps the last fifty.

theme.short: Light, dark, or follow the system. The choice is kept in this browser only.

independent.short: The chat agent in the Ask drawer. It is a separate Claude session that can read the dashboard and the repo to answer your questions.

idle.short: The agent is not doing anything right now. It finished its last step or is waiting for a message.
idle.more: Idle is normal between tasks. If an agent stays idle while a flow says it is working, it may be waiting on you or it may have stopped.

working.short: The agent ran a tool in the last few minutes, so it is busy on something now.

active.short: Same as working: the agent is busy right now, reading, writing or running commands.

testing.short: The agent is running tests or checks, for example a test suite, a linter or a type check.

waiting.short: Someone has to act before the work goes on. On a flow it means an ask waits for your answer; on an agent it means the agent waits for input.

blocked.short: The work cannot go on until something outside it changes, such as a missing access, a broken build or a decision.
blocked.more: An agent sets a step to blocked and should say why in the step. Often an ask follows that tells you what it needs.

done.short: Finished. For a flow step it means the agent says the step is complete; whether that is proven is a separate question (see claimed and verified).

pending.short: This step cannot start yet because it comes after an ask that is still open, or after an ask you answered No.
pending.more: Pending steps are dimmed in the chart. They wake up when you answer the ask, or when the agent changes the plan.

output.short: The view of a flow that tells its result visually: a picture first (a screenshot, the agent's diagram, or a chart drawn from the flow), what was built, and how to test it by hand, step by step.
output.more: It is where an opened flow lands. The agent fills it when a piece of work is finished; until then it shows what the flow's own proof has, marked auto. Request test steps asks the agent for the steps, and Request visuals for a picture too.

visual.short: The picture an opened flow leads with on Output. Every flow has one: the agent's screenshots, else its diagram of how it works, else a summary chart the dashboard draws from the flow's steps.
visual.more: The summary chart has at most 7 shapes: a solid box for done work, a dashed box for work left (orange when blocked), a diamond for each question with your answer on its arrow.

diagram.short: A small boxes and arrows picture of how a piece of work works, drawn by the agent with flow diagram when there is nothing to screenshot (an API, a job, a deploy).
diagram.more: It is the big picture only: at most 8 boxes with short names. A pill is a person or outside system, a box with a double top line is stored data, a diamond is a decision.

status.short: The view of a flow that lists where it stands: what is built and how well it is proven, what is still missing, and the questions that wait on you.
status.more: Click a step's title to see where it sits in the Process chart. A link that opens a flow at one step lands here.

test step.short: One thing to do by hand to check the work, with what you should see and a screenshot of it, written by the agent with flow test-step.
test step.more: The I saw this box beside each step is your own checklist: it is kept in this browser only and never changes the flow.

process.short: The view of a flow that shows how the work was done: the chart of every step, check and ask in order, with their links.
process.more: Click a step in the chart to open its drawer with the full evidence. The page remembers which view you used last.

unproven.short: The agent marked the step done but attached no evidence, so nothing shows it really happened.

claimed.short: The step is done and has evidence attached, such as a commit or a test line, but you have not checked it yet.

verified.short: You looked at the evidence and ticked the step. Only you can tick it; no agent or command can.
verified.more: This is the strongest proof state. Untick it if you change your mind.

sent.short: Your answer to an ask reached the agent that asked, through a short relay turn.

not delivered.short: Your answer is saved, but the relay could not hand it to the agent, usually because the agent is not running or its name did not match. Use retry.
not delivered.more: Hover the words to see the reason. The answer is never lost: it stays on the flow, and the agent reads it the next time it looks at the flow.

local.short: The code exists only on this machine, in a worktree or on the followup branch, and is not pushed to dev yet.

dev.short: The code is merged into origin/dev, the shared branch that deploys to the dev site for testing.

stage.short: The code is on origin/stage, the branch that deploys to the stage site, the last check before real users.

prod.short: Short for production. The code is on origin/main and is live for real users.
prod.more: Prod deploys are started by hand. A change there reaches real people, so it gets the most care.

step.short: A piece of work in a flow, such as writing a fix or running a migration. It has a status and can carry evidence.

check.short: A step whose whole job is to test something, such as a test run or a look at the dev site. It also carries evidence.

note.short: Plain text. In a flow chart it is a remark with no status; as evidence it is a written observation from the agent.

evidence.short: What an agent attaches to a step to show it was really done: a commit, a diff, a test line, a screenshot, a link or a note.

commit.short: A saved snapshot of changes in git, with a message saying what changed. As evidence it opens the commit and its diff.

diff.short: The lines that changed: red for removed, green for added. As evidence it shows the uncommitted changes in a worktree.

test.short: A test result as evidence: the line that says how many tests passed or failed, and sometimes the full output.

shot.short: A screenshot or short screen recording an agent took, often of the app in a browser, as evidence.

url.short: A web link as evidence, for example to a deployed page or a pull request.

worktree.short: A second working folder for the same git repo, on its own branch. Agents use one each so they can work at the same time without touching each other.
worktree.more: All worktrees share one history, so a commit made in one is visible from the others once it is on a shared branch.

branch.short: A named line of commits in git. Work happens on a branch and is merged into a shared one like dev when it is ready.

fast-forward.short: A merge where git only moves the branch pointer ahead, because the target has no commits of its own. No merge commit is made.
fast-forward.more: If both sides have new commits, a fast-forward is impossible and git needs a real merge instead.

merge base.short: The last commit two branches have in common. Git compares both sides against it to work out what each one changed.

origin.short: The usual name for the shared copy of the repo on GitHub. origin/dev means the dev branch as it is there, not on this machine.

followup.short: The branch the main checkout sits on in this repo. Work there counts as local until it is merged into dev.

headless turn.short: One run of Claude with no chat window: the dashboard gives it a prompt, waits for the answer and closes it.
headless turn.more: The dashboard uses short headless turns for the answer relay and for explaining text, each with only the tools it needs.

relay.short: The small helper that passes your answer to an ask on to the agent that asked, by a short headless turn that sends it a message.
relay.more: Answers to the same agent within 30 seconds go as one message, to save turns.

subagent.short: A helper session an agent starts for one task, such as a review. It reports back to the agent that started it and then stops.

coordinator.short: The coordinating session that hands out work and merges everyone's branches into dev.

pr.short: Pull request: a request on GitHub to merge one branch into another, where others review the changes first.

code review.short: Someone reads the changes before they are merged, to catch bugs and unclear code. On the Tickets page a chip shows whether a ticket was reviewed.

idempotent.short: Safe to run more than once: doing it twice ends the same as doing it once, so a retry cannot create duplicates.

sse.short: Server-Sent Events: a connection where the server keeps pushing updates to the page, as the chat does while Independent answers.

token.short: Either a secret string that proves who you are to a service, or a small piece of text a language model reads and writes. The context tells which.

mcp.short: Model Context Protocol: a standard way to give Claude extra tools, such as a browser or a ticket tracker.

playwright.short: A tool that drives a real web browser from code. Agents use it to click through the app and take screenshots as evidence.

switchboard.short: A ticket tracker the dashboard can read through an MCP tool. It reads the tickets and never changes them.

tracker.short: Any system that holds tickets and their status, such as Switchboard, Linear or Jira.

collection.short: One set of tickets the Tickets page can show, read from one source and optionally filtered to a range of ids.

source.short: Where a collection's tickets come from: a tracker read by an MCP tool, or an agent that reads a board in the browser.

verdict.short: Your call on a reviewed ticket: deliver now, after a dev check, after a doc fix, or not yet.

snapshot.short: A copy of the data as it was at one moment, kept so the page can show something at once while fresh data loads.

orchestration.short: The grid on the Tickets page: agents across, levels down, and each ticket in the cell for who built it and how far it got.

progress report.short: A short summary of what one agent did, built from its own transcript.

deploy.short: Putting a version of the code onto a running site, such as dev, stage or prod, so people can use it.

transcript.short: The full record of a Claude session: every message, tool call and result, saved by Claude Code on this machine.

waiting on you.short: The list of asks across all flows that have no answer yet. Each one holds up an agent until you answer it.

glossary.short: The page of every word the dashboard can explain: built in, learned from flows, saved by an agent, or written by you.
glossary.more: Hover a tinted word anywhere to read it. Your own wording always wins over the others.

story.short: The first block of a flow Output: a few plain lines of who did what, and why.
story.more: The agent writes them with flow say. When it wrote none, the dashboard makes a short one from the steps and marks it auto.

picture.short: The one visual a flow Output always shows: the result screenshots, the agent diagram of how it works, or a chart drawn from the steps.

how to test.short: The steps to try the work yourself, each with what you should see. Tick I saw this as you go; the ticks stay in this browser.

details.short: The folded-away part of a flow Output: the agent summary in full and the commits it made.

marked word.short: A technical word an agent wrote in square brackets. The page shows it tinted, and hovering it explains it.
marked word.more: Unknown marked words are looked up once, the first time their flow opens, and saved in the Glossary.

learned.short: A Glossary word the dashboard looked up by itself, in one small model turn, the first time a flow used it.
